# Energy Planet

> A free browser game built on Australia's real electricity market. Players run
> a power generation company: they buy real Australian power stations, keep
> them maintained, and earn the live AEMO wholesale spot price, which updates
> every five minutes. It is also a serious live dashboard of the Australian
> grid.

## What it is

- /play — the app. Five views:
  - POWER: live 3D map of Australia's grid. Generation vs demand columns per
    region, every major power station (real names, locations, fuels,
    capacities), interconnector flows, city supply arcs, satellite imagery on
    zoom.
  - PRICE: live wholesale spot price per region (AEMO 5-minute dispatch)
    against benchmark retail rates (DMO/VDO), with 7-day and 90-day history.
  - DESK: a paper-trading desk for a hypothetical flat-rate energy retailer —
    swaps and caps marked against the live spot, with backtesting and alerts.
  - BUILD: a stylised merit-order model of how new projects (e.g. Snowy 2.0)
    or coal closures (e.g. Eraring) would shift regional prices and the
    generation mix.
  - OPS: the game. Start with $500m, buy stations, maintain them (panel
    cleaning, turbine gearboxes, coal deliveries, cell balancing), earn the
    live spot price. Each site renders as an isometric pixel-art diorama with
    an X-ray inspection mode.
- /login — passwordless email sign-in. Accounts add cross-device cloud saves
  and a public leaderboard ranked by company value. Guest play needs no
  account (saves in the browser).

## Data

- Sources: AEMO public dashboard feeds and OpenElectricity (formerly OpenNEM),
  both refreshed every 5 minutes, covering the five NEM regions (QLD, NSW,
  VIC, SA, TAS) and Western Australia's SWIS.
- The trading, maintenance economics and price-impact modelling are
  simulations for play and education. Nothing connects to any real market
  system. Not financial advice. Not affiliated with AEMO.

## Tech

Next.js App Router, three.js (react-globe.gl + custom isometric scenes),
Supabase (optional accounts), deployed on Vercel. Open data, no tracking
beyond basic analytics.
